n07139d08a59.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rashtrakuta king Krishna III?
o: He helped Danarnava kill the Eastern Chalukya ruler Ammaraja II
The killing of Ammaraja II took place in 970 CE
Vengi was seized after the killing of Ammaraja II
The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved during his reign
n07139d08a59.x: Krishna III helped Danarnava kill Ammaraja II in 970 CE and seize Vengi. The Kailasa temple was carved under Krishna I, not Krishna III.

nee45c4b5076.s: Which of the following Ellora caves is the latest in date?
nee45c4b5076.x: The order is Dashavatara, Ravan ki Khai, Dumar Lena and then Kailasa, so Kailasa is the latest of the four.

n66acc65be03.s:
Consider the following statements about the Badami Chalukya rulers:
1. Pulakesin I ruled before Kirtivarman I.
2. Mangalesha ruled before Kirtivarman I.
3. Vikramaditya I ruled after Mangalesha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n66acc65be03.x: The order is Pulakesin I, Kirtivarman I, Mangalesha (regent) and Vikramaditya I. Mangalesha came after Kirtivarman I, so statement 2 is wrong.

nee7e6b6791e.s:
Consider the following statements about Pulakesin II's eastern campaign:
1. He conquered Kosala and Kalinga before marching to Vengi.
2. He appointed Kubja Vishnuvardhana at Vengi before defeating the Durjayas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
nee7e6b6791e.x: Pulakesin II conquered Kosala and Kalinga, marched to Vengi, defeated the Durjayas and only then appointed Kubja Vishnuvardhana.

ne4284b8ae96.s: Which of the following Chalukya-Pallava rounds is NOT correctly matched with its rulers?
o: First round – Pulakesin II and Narasimhavarman I
Second round – Pulakesin II and Narasimhavarman I
Third round – Vikramaditya I and the Pallavas
Fourth round – Vikramaditya II and Nandivarman II
ne4284b8ae96.x: The first round was fought between Pulakesin II and Mahendravarman I; Narasimhavarman I was his opponent in the second round.

new.s: The vimana (tower) of the Kailasa temple at Ellora is built in which style?
new.x: Kailasa has a three-tiered Dravida vimana, even though it stands in Nagara territory in Maharashtra.

new.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved top-down from a single cliff of which rock?
new.x: Kailasa is a monolithic temple carved top-down from a single basalt cliff.

new.s: Which cave is the only chaitya at Ellora?
new.x: Cave 10 is the only chaitya at Ellora; Cave 16 is Kailasa and Cave 32 is the Jain Indra Sabha.

new.s: The Indra Sabha (Cave 32) at Ellora belongs to which group?
new.x: Indra Sabha, Cave 32, is a Jain (Digambara) cave of the Jain group, caves 30-34.

new.s: Which group of caves is the earliest at Ellora?
new.x: The Buddhist caves (1-12) are the earliest, c. 600-730 CE, before the Rashtrakutas; the Jain caves are the latest.

new.s: Many historians date the main Elephanta cave with the Trimurti to which dynasty?
new.x: Though an MPPSC key credited it to the Rashtrakutas, many historians date the main Elephanta cave to the 6th-century Kalachuris.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Elephanta caves:
1. They form an island cave complex near Mumbai.
2. Their masterpiece is the three-headed Shiva known as Trimurti.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Elephanta is an island cave complex near Mumbai, and its masterpiece is the Trimurti (Maheshamurti).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rashtrakuta religious policy?
o: The early rulers were staunch Shaivas
Jainism reached its peak under Amoghavarsha I
Buddhists were persecuted by the rulers
Arab merchants were allowed to build mosques
new.x: Vaishnavism and Buddhism received royal patronage and there was no persecution.

new.s: The Arab title 'Balhara' for the Rashtrakuta king is derived from which title?
new.x: Balhara is the Arabic form of the Rashtrakuta title Vallabha (Vallabharaja).

new.s: Which of the following traveller – Rashtrakuta king pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Sulaiman wrote in the reign of Amoghavarsha I; Al-Masudi visited c. 915-16 CE under Indra III.

new.s: In Rashtrakuta administration, the Rashtra (province) was headed by the:
new.x: The Rashtra was under the Rashtrapati; the Vishaya under the Vishayapati, the Bhukti under the Bhogapati and the Grama under the Gramakuta.

new.s: In Rashtrakuta administration, the Bhogapati was the head of the:
new.x: The Bhukti, a unit smaller than the Vishaya, was headed by the Bhogapati.

new.s: The Rashtrakutas imported horses by sea from:
new.x: Horses were imported by sea from Arabia, while textiles were exported.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Rashtrakuta trade:
1. Cambay, Thana and Sopara were western ports.
2. Arab merchants were barred from settling in the western ports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Cambay, Thana and Sopara were western ports; Arab merchants lived peacefully there and were not barred.

new.s: The Rashtrakuta era raised which language to a classical literary medium?
new.x: The Rashtrakuta era raised Kannada to a classical medium.

new.s: Vatapi, the Badami Chalukya capital, is in which district of Karnataka?
new.x: Vatapi is modern Badami in Bagalkot district, set in sandstone hills around Agastya lake.

new.s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler, the real founder of the dynasty, performed the Ashvamedha sacrifice?
new.x: Pulakesin I (543-566) was the real founder; he performed the Ashvamedha and walled Vatapi.

new.s: Kirtivarman I's Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma sacrifice is recorded in the:
new.x: The Mahakuta pillar records Kirtivarman I's Bahusuvarna-Agnishtoma sacrifice.

new.s: Who was the last ruler of the Badami Chalukya dynasty?
new.x: Kirtivarman II (746-753) was the last Badami Chalukya ruler, overthrown by Dantidurga.

new.s: The Eastern Chalukyas, who became independent at Vengi in 624 CE, had their capital at:
new.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana made Vengi independent in 624 CE, founding the Eastern Chalukyas with their capital at Pithapuram.

new.s: The first gold coins of South India are credited to:
new.x: Pulakesin II is credited with the first South Indian gold coins.

new.s: Ravikirti, the composer of the Aihole inscription, followed which faith?
new.x: Ravikirti was a Jain court poet of Pulakesin II, and the inscription is on the Meguti Jain temple.

new.s: Pishtapura, listed among Pulakesin II's victories in the Aihole inscription, is modern:
new.x: The Aihole inscription lists Kosala, Kalinga and Pishtapura (Pithapuram) among the victories.

new.s: Which of the following is an inscription of Kubja Vishnuvardhana in Andhra?
new.x: Chipurupalli is among Kubja Vishnuvardhana's inscriptions; Maruturu, Aihole and Lohnara belong to Pulakesin II.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chalukya-Harsha conflict:
1. It is known from the Aihole inscription and Hiuen Tsang.
2. It is recorded in the Kailasanatha inscription.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Narmada victory is known from the Aihole inscription and Hiuen Tsang, not the Kailasanatha inscription.

new.s: For about how many years did the Pallavas occupy Vatapi after 642 CE?
new.x: The Pallavas held Vatapi from 642 to c. 655, about 13 years, until Vikramaditya I recovered it.

new.s: The Badami Chalukyas were finally replaced by the:
new.x: The Rashtrakutas under Dantidurga replaced the Badami Chalukyas, not the Cholas.

new.s: Who won the Battle of Manimangala (c. 642 CE)?
new.x: Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakesin II at Manimangala, as also at Pariyala and Suramara.

new.s: Vatapi was sacked in 642 CE by which Pallava general?
new.x: Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi in 642, and it was sacked by his general Paranjoti.

new.s: Pulakesin II's title Dakshinapatheshwara was set against which title of Harsha?
new.x: Pulakesin II was Dakshinapatheshwara, lord of the south, against Harsha's Uttarapatheshwara.

new.s: The inscription Vikramaditya II left on a pillar at Kanchi is in which language?
new.x: Vikramaditya II left a Kannada inscription on a pillar at Kanchi.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vikramaditya II's occupation of Kanchi?
o: It took place in Nandivarman II's reign
He gave gold to the Rajasimheshvara temple
new.x: Vikramaditya II did not plunder Kanchi; he gave gold to the Rajasimheshvara (Kailasanatha) temple.

new.s: Under the Badami Chalukyas, agraharas (Brahmin land grants) were run by the:
new.x: Agraharas were Brahmin land grants run by mahajanas.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Badami Chalukya administration:
1. The vishaya was a district under the vishayapati.
2. The Rashtrakutas were among its feudatories.
3. Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: vishaya under the vishayapati, Rashtrakutas among the feudatories, and Vatapi and Aihole as urban and trade centres.

new.s: Which Kalyani Chalukya princess governed Kisukad?
new.x: The Kalyani Chalukya princess Akkadevi governed Kisukad.

new.s: Kumkumdevi, sister of Vikramaditya I, granted a village to a:
new.x: Kumkumdevi granted a village to a Jain monastery.
